data.content:
Plan review: APPROVED with two refinements.

Completeness vs acceptance criteria: AC1 step 3, AC2 step 2, AC3 step 2b + step 5, AC4 step 1 + step 5, AC5 step 1 (shared guard extraction keeps bare rollback byte-identical), AC6 step 4, AC7 step 6. No gaps.

Feasibility confirmed against the tree, not assumed: workflow_runtime::next_outcome_state (src/workflow_runtime.rs:112) already resolves failure maps and is unreferenced by CLI code; loom 0.3.0 is installed and a fresh build restores the Failure Modes body, so the bundle work is regeneration rather than authoring; FileLock (src/locks.rs) is non-reentrant, which is what forces the single-locked-section design instead of composing existing App methods.

Refinement 1 - escape-state outcomes. The shipment failure map declares release_blocked -> blocked, an escape state rather than a queue state. The resolver must handle a non-queue target: still clear the lease and close the step as failed, and set blocked_from_state correctly (src/app/state_ops.rs:254 next_blocked_from_state) so hierarchy ranking stays right. Add a test for release_blocked alongside merge_conflicts.

Refinement 2 - dry-run semantics. --outcome must compose with --dry-run: resolve and print the target without mutating state or lease. Assert dry-run leaves lease_id and lease state untouched, since that is the same no-partial-mutation guarantee AC4 demands.

No security concerns: the change narrows rather than widens mutation authority because targets come from the compiled workflow map, never from caller input. Maintainability concern noted and already mitigated by the plan: state_ops.rs at 437 lines is near the 500-line ceiling, so the new path lands in src/app/state_fail_ops.rs.

No child knots needed; splitting would break the single-write atomicity the tests assert.
